title: Playing in Korea's cold
summary: Valves and bell freezing, gloves and breathing through the horn.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: When you played your performances, did you then change?

You'd wash up and change and everything. But then it was pretty cold there, too, boy. Pshew! It was something else. We had to get out and play in the cold! Man, my bell used to freeze in between choruses. And I'd be banging on it, trying to get it to move, blowing my breath through it and all that. You had to keep doing that all the time in that cold weather, because they'll freeze up in a minute.
Did you ever play with gloves on?
Oh yeah! Heck, yeah. Are you kiddin'? Shee-it. I had gloves on and mittens and everything else I could get to play, man. Boy, it was pretty cold in Korea.
And you had to worry about the horn freezing to your lips, too.

Yeah, I had to worry about that. Well, if you keep blowing on the mouthpiece then it can't freeze, because your hot breath will keep it warm, you know. But boy, the valves you've got to keep working, too, because if you just let them sit there for a minute, they just go...

Yeah, they freeze right up. And then you have to blow and blow and blow until you get them... So if you've got a chorus (?), you just take the mouthpiece and keep playing, and like you play that chorus yourself.
That's the only way to keep going.
